content:
anya: FYI noticed a big initial-paint hang on dashboards after today's canary. SparseWidget takes ~3.5s before first chart draws when >200 series. telemetry spike at 11:04 UTC: https://telemetry.redwood/heat/1738003456 :eyes:

sam: ugh. is this the kvcache eviction we saw last week or a bundle parse? any console logs?

anya: console shows repeated `ChunkLoadError` for `sparse-widget-async` in first 2s, but then it parses and main thread jams while building series frames. sample trace attached (short): `main.js:frameBuild 1200ms -> renderSeries 2100ms`

jin: did we change splitpoints in the canary? I pushed a tweak to `split-config` yesterday to inline a tiny helper.

mira: deploy-bot reported the canary rollout: `canary 2024.03.2 -> 15% route weight` at 11:00. deploy-bot: canary finished step 1 -> partial traffic.

deploy-bot: canary 2024.03.2 started at 10:58 UTC; routing weight updated to 15% across eu/us regions.

anya: The interesting bit — the affected sessions are mostly new users (cold kvcache). When kvcache miss + async chunk load -> long JS parse (looks like bundle bloat), which stalls scheduling for the worker pool.

sam: can we replicate with `--prefetch=false` locally? Maybe prefetch policy changed.

anya: repro script I used: `curl -H "x-redwood-session: new" https://console.int/metrics?dashboard=sparse-large` then open devtools and spam refresh. Repro is consistent.

jin: quick check: bundle size diff on canary -> `+47KB` in `sparse-widget-async` (+3.4%); added `series-quant` util. Could that trigger slower parse for certain V8 buckets?

mira: telemetry-bot: sampling rate for dashboard load traces jumped from 1% to 10% in canary region (testing). Might be overwhelming client tracing lib and causing parse/serialize overhead. telemetry-bot: flagging high ingestion events.

sam: two hypotheses: (1) splitpoint change + small bundle bump causes slow parse on low-end CPUs, (2) telemetry sampling + extra trace sync causes main thread work to balloon. Both plausible and compounding with kvcache miss.

jin: simple mitigation: revert inline of `series-quant` and restore previous splitpoint. I can roll a tiny patch and cut a canary hotfix.

anya: can we also lower telemetry sampling for canary users while we debug? The large trace payloads look synchronous.

mira: I can flip sampling back to 1% for canary cohort. Doing now -> `telemetry service: set sampling=1% for tag:canary-2024-03-2`

mira: done. will take ~30s to propagate.

sam: Jin — if you have the revert ready, let's do a canary rollback to 5% route weight and then promote if green. We need to avoid user-facing regressions.

jin: pushing patch now. version 2024.03.2-hotfix1. Rolling to canary at 11:18 with 5% weight.

deploy-bot: deploy 2024.03.2-hotfix1 started -> canary 5% at 11:18 UTC.

anya: after hotfix: initial paint for repro sessions drops to ~450ms. Confirmed by local run and telemetry. Nice.

sam: follow-ups: 1) add guarded async trace serialization (make it non-blocking), 2) add low-end CPU test in perf CI for any bundle parse changes, 3) add a kvcache warmup for dashboard entry route.

mira: filed follow-up issues: PERF-1229 (trace-serialize async), PERF-1230 (ci low-end parse test), PERF-1231 (kvcache warmup route).

anya: moving to postmortem notes channel — but leaving this thread for rollout coordination. thanks all :thumbsup:

jin: thanks — will keep an eye on alerting.

telemetry-bot: Alert cleared for high ingestion for canary cohort at 11:32 UTC.
